POSH_POLICY.//: A policy is unilateral: no second participant, and the general-provisions baseline is suppressed because notice, assignment, counterparts and force majeure have no meaning in an instrument with no counterparty.

REFUND_AND_CANCELLATION_POLICY.//: Published to consumers, not agreed with them. The general-provisions baseline is suppressed: assignment, counterparts and force majeure have no meaning in a policy, and a force-majeure clause in a consumer refund policy reads as an attempt to excuse non-performance.

SHIPPING_AND_DELIVERY_POLICY.//: Published to consumers, not agreed with them. The general-provisions baseline is suppressed: assignment, counterparts and force majeure have no meaning in a policy, and a force-majeure clause in a consumer refund policy reads as an attempt to excuse non-performance.

PROMISSORY_NOTE.//: A promissory note is a short unilateral instrument. The general-provisions baseline is suppressed: force majeure, counterparts and assignment clauses would destroy its character as a negotiable instrument, and Section 4 requires the promise to be UNCONDITIONAL.

POWER_OF_ATTORNEY.//: A power of attorney is a unilateral deed executed by the Principal alone. The general-provisions baseline is suppressed: a deed of authority has no counterparty to give notice to, nothing to assign, and no counterparts.

TERM_SHEET.//: The general-provisions baseline is suppressed, by baselineClauseIds: [] (D4.44). Until 9 Oct 2026 this note said so while the data did not: the policy inherited the thirteen general provisions from defaults, and every term sheet shipped force majeure, assignment, waiver, severability, entire agreement (superseding 'term sheets'), further assurance and counterparts. The constraint rules already excluded TERM_SHEET, so validation never asked for them and never noticed they were there.

generation.//: AI tailoring is off for this instrument. Whether a provision binds turns on its exact wording, and a model asked to make text read naturally turns 'it is proposed that the Investor will' into 'the Investor shall'. The coherence checks would catch it; not generating it is better.

//: D4.44. The instrument is described here, as knowledge, and the engine reads it: the opening, the recitals, the noun the document uses for itself, which provisions bind, the terms a term sheet must state, and the economic choices that must come from an answer.

binding_character: BINDING | PARTLY_BINDING | NON_BINDING. provision_status maps clause ids to BINDING_NOW | NON_BINDING; a clause in the document that is not listed is UNRESOLVED_PENDING_REVIEW, and the coherence checks report it.

recitals: a. The Investor proposes to invest in the Company, and the Company and the Founders wish to record the principal terms on which that investment is proposed (the "Investment").

b. Except for the Binding Provisions identified in the provision headed "Status of this Term Sheet", this Term Sheet is not legally binding, and the Investment is subject to the execution of Definitive Agreements.

input_checks.message: The investment amount and the pre-money valuation must be positive amounts.
The number of shares outstanding on a fully diluted basis must be a whole number above zero.
The option pool must be a percentage above 0 and below 100.
A liquidation preference multiple must be above zero. Choose 'No liquidation preference' if none is intended.

in: Counted before the investment (dilutes existing shareholders only)
Created after the investment (dilutes all shareholders, including the Investor)

input_checks.message: Give the size of the option pool, or choose that no option pool is proposed.
Give the liquidation preference multiple, or choose that there is no liquidation preference.
The date this Term Sheet lapses must be after the date of the Term Sheet.
State the exclusivity period as a length of time, for example '45 days' or 'sixty days'.
A liquidation preference below 1x is unusual: the Investor would be entitled to less than it invested before other shareholders are paid. It is not invalid; check that it is intended.
A liquidation preference above 2x is unusual and can leave founders and employees with little or nothing on a modest exit.
An exclusivity period over 90 days is unusual; 30 to 60 days is common. A long period keeps the Company from other investors while the Investor is not committed.
An exclusivity period over 180 days should be reviewed by an advocate for reasonableness under Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
An option pool above 20 per cent of fully diluted capital is unusual.
The investment is larger than the pre-money valuation, so the Investor would hold a majority after the Investment. Check that this is intended; it changes who controls the Company.

A non-resident investor brings the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 into play, including pricing, sectoral and reporting requirements. Have an advocate confirm the structure.
Have an advocate confirm whether these debentures fall outside the definition of 'deposit' under the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014.

Equity shares carry no preferential right on a winding up (Section 43 of the Companies Act, 2013). A preference on equity shares can operate only as an arrangement among shareholders; have an advocate confirm how it would work.

For a non-resident investor, any adjustment to the conversion price must still satisfy the pricing requirements of the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019. Have an advocate confirm the mechanism.

ESOP_GRANT_LETTER.//: A grant letter is a short instrument issued under a scheme that carries the general terms. The baseline is suppressed so the letter does not restate them and drift out of step with the scheme it is subject to.

naming.//: A notice is written in the second person: "my client" and "you", not "the Sender" and "the Addressee". Those two words were listed as aliases here, and the role-normalising pass duly rewrote them into the canonical labels - turning "Should you fail to concur" into "Should Addressee fail to concur", which reads like a bad translation and also defeated the check that a notice must state a consequence. Canonical labels only; the pronouns are left alone.

hardening.//: A notice is a letter, not a deed. It has no severability clause, no force majeure clause and no counterparts clause, because it is not a bargain whose terms could be severed, excused or signed in parts. The thirteen general provisions that every agreement carries are therefore switched off here rather than being carried and then apologised for.
